title: Coralee bell pepper (Coralee F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Coralee bell pepper is an F1 hybrid bell pepper variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Coralee bell pepper is an F1 hybrid bell pepper variety, also sold or known as Coralee F1. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Coralee bell pepper is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Coralee F1, this is the same bell pepper. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [bell pepper variety finder](/crop-varieties/bell-pepper), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit bell pepper fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 60 to 70 days after transplanting.
Tolerant to aphids, leafminer, thrips, broad mites, bacterial wilt and anthracnose (seller's claim).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: in Ramgo's bell pepper line, only the seller's page found. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual bell pepper on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Coralee bell pepper

Bell pepper does best in cool places such as Benguet and Bukidnon. In the lowlands, pick a heat tolerant hybrid and grow it in the dry season under some shade. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.

items.q: Is Coralee F1 the same as Coralee?
items.a: Yes. Coralee F1 is another name for Coralee. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Coralee?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
